name: The Immaculate Conception
history: The Church teaches that Mary, by a singular grace of God and in view of the merits of Christ, was preserved free from all stain of original sin from the first moment of her conception. Pius IX defined the dogma in 1854; four years later Our Lady told Bernadette at Lourdes, 'I am the Immaculate Conception.'
prayer: O Mary, conceived without sin, pray for us who have recourse to thee.
meditation: Tota pulchra es, Maria. Ask her to help you hate one particular sin.
life: The feast of Mary's conception was kept in the East from about the eighth century, and in England it was celebrated at Winchester and Canterbury before the Norman Conquest. Theologians long debated how Mary could be free of original sin when all are redeemed by Christ. The Franciscan John Duns Scotus answered that she was redeemed in a more perfect way, preserved from sin rather than freed from it, in view of her Son's merits. Pope Sixtus IV approved the feast in 1476, and Clement XI extended it to the whole Church in 1708. On 8 December 1854 Pius IX defined the doctrine as revealed by God, in the bull Ineffabilis Deus. At Lourdes in 1858 the Lady told Bernadette her name, words the Church has approved as private revelation. In many countries today is a holy day of obligation.
prayerTo: Immaculate Virgin Mary, all fair and full of grace, God preserved you from every stain of sin to be the worthy Mother of His Son. Look kindly on me, a sinner. Help me to hate sin and love purity of heart, and lead me by your prayers to the Saviour who redeemed you first and redeems us all. Amen.
penance: Go to Mass and, if you can, to Confession this Advent. Pray 'O Mary, conceived without sin, pray for us who have recourse to thee' each time you are tempted today.
